NIN & Boys Noize Tribute Night is an industrial/electronic music celebration happening at The X-Bar in Cupertino on July 18th, 2026. Plastic DiseaseBased on the industrial/EBM focus of the night, Plastic Disease likely specializes in dark electronic sounds, industrial beats, and the aggressive, mechanical soundscapes that define the Nine Inch Nails aesthetic. They'll be bringing the raw, distorted energy that fans of industrial music crave.

A dinner featuring Buffalo Trace whiskies paired with a multi-course menu.
Buffalo Trace Distillery, nestled along the banks of the Kentucky River in Frankfort, is celebrated for its rich history and exceptional bourbon craftsmanship. Established in 1773, it stands as one of the oldest continually operating distilleries in the United States. Today, it remains a benchmark in American whiskey, producing a remarkable portfolio that includes its flagship Buffalo Trace Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey, Colonel E.H. Taylor Jr. Bourbons, and the legendary Van Winkle whiskeys.
We are delighted to welcome Andrew Marks, Sazerac Portfolio Manager, who will guide guests through the history of this storied distillery while presenting an extraordinary tasting, featuring rare bottlings such as Van Winkle 12 Year and George T. Stagg Barrel Proof Bourbon from the coveted Buffalo Trace Antique Collection.

events.title: Leonardo Art Science Evening Rendezvous (LASER) at The Hub
events.description_preview: A special LASER to celebrate Stanford Research Park's 75th anniversary. Join us at The Hub at Stanfo...
events.description_detail:
A special LASER to celebrate Stanford Research Park's 75th anniversary. Join us at The Hub at Stanford Research Park. #SRP
The LASERs (Leonardo Art Science Evening Rendezvous) are an international program of evening gatherings that bring artists and scientists together for informal presentations and conversation with an audience. This evening, chaired by cultural historian Piero Scaruffi, will be a special LASER to celebrate the Stanford Research Park, that was founded 75 years ago.
The evening will open with a brief video interview with a Silicon Valley engineer of the 1960s: John Minck.
It will be followed by four talks:
- Mihai Codreanu (Google) on "The Impact of University Research Parks"
- Piero Scaruffi (Stanford) on "A History of Silicon Valley"
- Elise DeMarzo (City of Palo Alto) on "Digital Art, Real Community"
- Ge Wang (Stanford) on "What Do We (Really) Want from AI?"
Mihai Codreanu is an economist working on tracking innovation and technology development over the very long-run. His Stanford dissertation focused on university research parks, and Stanford Research Park in particular.
Piero Scaruffi has worked on Internet and Artificial Intelligence technologies since the early 1980s and has written "A History of Silicon Valley" (2011), which has also been translated in China.
Elise DeMarzo is the Director of Public Art for the City of Palo Alto and oversees all aspects of both temporary and permanent public art installations. She implemented a new media public art festival called Code:ART in 2017.
Ge Wang is an Associate Professor at Stanford University's Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA), director of the Stanford Laptop Orchestra, and the author of "Artful Design: Technology in Search of the Sublime".
Detailed bios at: http://www.lasertalks.com/
Attendance is open to all. Please register to help us plan seating and refreshments.

events.title: CASPA × IEEE 2026 Summer Symposium
events.description_preview: Paving the AI Superhighway: Where Power Meets Intelligence 📅 Date: Saturday, July 18th, 2026 ⏰ Time...
events.description_detail:
Paving the AI Superhighway: Where Power Meets Intelligence
📅 Date: Saturday, July 18th, 2026
⏰ Time: 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM
📍 Venue: Intel SC-12 Auditorium, 3600 Juliette Ln, Santa Clara, CA 95054
As we enter the era of superintelligence, advanced power delivery and energy efficiency have transcended foundational infrastructure to become the ultimate drivers for scaling artificial intelligence. Addressing this critical paradigm shift requires comprehensive innovation across the entire semiconductor power ecosystem, spanning advanced materials, high-density power electronics, and rack-scale hyperscale infrastructure optimization.
Co-hosted by CASPA and IEEE (Santa Clara Valley Section & San Francisco Bay Area Power Electronics Society), the 2026 Summer Symposium will examine the advanced power and connectivity technologies essential for the AI era. Presenting a distinguished panel of technology executives, esteemed researchers, and industry pioneers from top-tier semiconductor, power electronics, and cloud computing organizations, this premier event aims to foster critical dialogues on how the rapid expansion of AI is fundamentally reshaping the global power and semiconductor landscape.
We warmly invite you to join us to:
Explore cutting-edge innovations in high-density power architectures, advanced power electronics, and efficient thermal management systems.
Engage with leading visionaries on the structural power challenges facing next-generation hyperscale AI computing.
Connect with a vibrant community of over 9,000 CASPA and 10,400 IEEE Santa Clara Valley Section members to expand your professional network across the semiconductor and AI ecosystems.
We look forward to welcoming you for an inspiring afternoon of technical insight, strategic discussion, and high-value networking. Let’s collaborate to build the foundation of the AI era!
Santa Clara, CA 95054

events.description_preview:
Sacrament Meeting

You're invited to our weekly worship service. This is a ...
events.description_detail:
Sacrament Meeting

You're invited to our weekly worship service. This is a time when our whole congregation comes together to pray, sing hymns, hear uplifting messages from fellow members, and most importantly, to remember Jesus Christ through the sacrament (similar to Communion in other Christian churches).

During the sacrament, we quietly reflect on His life and sacrifice as we take a small piece of bread and a cup of water, symbolizing His body and blood. It’s a peaceful moment to reset and think about how we can follow Him more closely in the coming week.

As a visitor, you’re welcome to simply observe and participate however you feel comfortable—no pressure at all.

Second Hour of Learning

After the main worship service, we offer a second hour of small-group classes for all ages:

  • Children (ages 3–11) go to Primary to learn about Jesus through songs, stories, and fun lessons.
  • Teens join age-based classes to talk about the gospel in ways that relate to them.
  • Adults rotate between Sunday School (scripture study together) and classes for men (Elders Quorum) and women (Relief Society) on alternating weeks.

Not sure where to go? Just ask anyone—we’d be happy to help you!

events.title: AI Supply Chain Hackathon 2026: Food Banks + AI
events.description_preview: Join our AI Supply Chain Hackathon and help to brainstorm and build solutions for adapting to the im...
events.description_detail:
Join our AI Supply Chain Hackathon and help to brainstorm and build solutions for adapting to the impact of supply chain disruption events!
Join us for the 3rd Annual AI Supply Chain Hackathon! This exciting event is happening in San Francisco with the option to join online, so you can participate from the comfort of your own home or workplace. For 2026, all judges will be in person and all team must have one representative onsite at Pebblebed, located at 1417 15th Street.
Supply chain disruptions can both create and amplify human suffering and degrades the fabric of collective life. Last year this Hackathon focused on weather, and the year before we focused on the supply chain for cancer drugs. In 2026, our Hackathon will focus on the impact of supply chains on Food Banks as an essential collective response layer to extreme disaster events, as well as the topic of chronic hunger across the US.
This Hackathon brings together stakeholders from the tech, policymaking, AI, and public sector communities to build solutions. Teams may create and demo their own AI/software OR propose a novel policy/cooperation solution.
You do not need to be technical or have a background in AI to participate, and we love teams that bring together cross-functional backgrounds spanning supply chain and procurement, policy, academia, and tech industry experience.
Audience Award - $1500
This unique event gives AI practitioners and early stage startup teams the chance to work side by side with supply chain and procurement professionals to help develop AI agents for supply chain operations at Food Banks.
With a panel of expert judges from industry, policymakers and nonprofits, the AI Supply Chain Hackathon is a terrific opportunity for people excited and concerned about the impact of AI on accelerating both supply chain decisions and supply chain disruptions.
